question: Delirium Tremens typically develops within 6–12 hours of the last drink in a habitual alcohol user.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The 6–12 hour window describes early withdrawal symptoms, not DT. Full Delirium Tremens — with delirium, autonomic hyperactivity, and hallucinations — typically begins 48–72 hours after cessation of alcohol in a dependent person. This timeline is critical in a custody death scenario.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — DT does NOT develop at 6–12 hours. Early withdrawal symptoms (tremor, anxiety, diaphoresis) begin at 6–24 hours, seizures at 12–48 hours, but the full syndrome of Delirium Tremens characteristically emerges at 48–72 hours after the last drink.
